framework_note: ATI's 10-K narrative is STRUCTURALLY OPPOSITE to the J-Book divergence target pattern. The canonical target (e.g., IonQ/YSS) names a SPECIFIC Pentagon PE (e.g., 0603287F) and claims it drives 80-96% of revenue; the J-Book then shows that PE zeroed for 2+ FYs. ATI instead claims GENERIC defense exposure (titanium, nickel alloys, zirconium/hafnium) sold through aerospace primes (Boeing, GE Aviation, Safran, RR, P&W) with diversified end-applications (naval nuclear, military jet engines, rotorcraft, armor, munitions). No PE numbers, no named DoD program-of-record drives a quantified revenue line. This means pentagon_jbook correctly resolves most claims to NOT_FOUND -> UNVERIFIABLE. That is the FRAMEWORK CORRECTLY PASSING a diversified materials supplier rather than red-flagging it. Substring 'matches' on contractor_name='ATI' (e.g., matched 'sofISTICATED', 'iniATIve', 'aviATIon'-style noise) were inspected and the matched programs do NOT list ATI/Allegheny as a contractor; rescored as NOT_FOUND.

scores.claim_text: A&D = ~68% of total sales in FY 2025.
supports: pentagon_jbook contractor lookups on 'ATI Inc.' and 'Allegheny Technologies' returned NOT_FOUND in corpus; ATI is a diversified specialty materials supplier sold to primes, not a J-Book line-item contractor
scores.interpretation: Concentration claim is at the END-MARKET level (commercial aero + defense), not at the PE level. The J-Book corpus does not list ATI as a primary contractor on any PE. This is the expected outcome for a materials-tier supplier; the claim is corroborated by EPA-FRS facility footprint (16 PA + 8 OR + 1 FL facilities verified active) and historic USAspending sub-tier titanium contracts (Allegheny Ludlum W15QKN08C0452, '6A1-4V TITANIUM'). No J-Book divergence signal.

scores.claim_text: Defense product sales grew 14% in FY 2025; HPMC defense +24%; expects continued growth.
supports: pentagon_jbook contractor='ATI' returned 4 substring-noise matches (LRDR/Lockheed; Cyber Security/Lockheed; SOF Tech Dev/Berry Aviation; Safety Program Mgmt/ARES) — none list ATI/Allegheny as contractor; rescored NOT_FOUND
scores.M_value: Apparent FUNDED_SHRINKING but on substring-noise matches (e.g., aviATIon, iniTIATIve); rescored to NOT_FOUND
scores.interpretation: Forward-growth assertion is end-market level. Corpus has no ATI-attributed program; cannot directly verify forward DoD demand. Reorganization caveat does not apply (no replacement_program). Treat as UNVERIFIABLE per heuristic #7 (NOT_FOUND != red flag for non-PE-specific claim).

scores.claim_text: ATI supplies materials for naval nuclear products (zirconium, hafnium, specialty alloys).
supports: pentagon_jbook does not have Columbia-class / Virginia-class / 'naval nuclear' SSN programs in the FY26 RDT&E + procurement corpus (the corpus covers 410 PEs but is weighted toward DARPA/MDA/SOCOM/AF/SF RDT&E + procurement, not Navy SCN naval-nuclear lines)
scores.interpretation: Naval nuclear (zirconium / hafnium for reactor cores) is a well-known forward-funded NAVSEA/NR program area, but it sits in the SCN (Shipbuilding & Conversion, Navy) and Naval Reactors line items, which are outside this corpus's coverage scope. Per heuristic #7, NOT_FOUND on outside-corpus claim = UNVERIFIABLE, NOT a red flag. EPA-FRS confirms the Millersburg OR zirconium/hafnium facility actually exists.

scores.claim_text: ATI has a long-term titanium airframe LTA with Boeing.
supports: pentagon_jbook contractor='Boeing' matched 'Technology Maturation Initiatives' which lists Boeing among multiple primes — this is a generic R&D umbrella, not directly tied to ATI titanium airframe LTA

Counterparty disclosure check via edgar_fts on Boeing CIK returned 0 hits for the exact phrase 'ATI Inc' (note: edgar_fts is exact-phrase brittle; Boeing's 10-Ks may reference 'Allegheny' or 'titanium suppliers' instead). Not a divergence signal.
scores.M_value: pentagon_jbook: 1 noise match on broad PE (Boeing is a prime on hundreds of programs); edgar_fts: 0 hits (exact-phrase limitation)
scores.interpretation: Boeing LTA is plausible at face value: Boeing buys titanium broadly. The J-Book pattern doesn't apply because the LTA is a commercial-airframe supply contract (777/787/737) plus some defense pull-through, not a specific PE-driven defense program. This is exactly the kind of broad-spectrum supplier relationship the J-Book test is NOT designed to flag. PASS.

scores.claim_text: ATI has LTAs with GE Aviation and Safran for jet engine alloys.
supports: pentagon_jbook(contractor_name='GE Aviation') and (contractor_name='Safran') both return NOT_FOUND — these engine OEMs supply hundreds of military and commercial platforms; the corpus tracks PE-level RDT&E/procurement lines, not engine-OEM contractor coverage at this granularity
scores.interpretation: LTA is primarily commercial aero (LEAP, GE9X) with military pull-through (F404, F414, T408). Heuristic #7: NOT_FOUND on a broad-spectrum engine OEM's component supplier is UNVERIFIABLE in strict reading but functionally PASS because the underlying engine programs are well-funded commercial + military families. No PE-divergence signal.

scores.claim_text: ATI has LTAs with Rolls-Royce and Pratt & Whitney for engine forgings.
supports: pentagon_jbook(contractor_name='Pratt & Whitney') and ('Rolls-Royce') both returned NOT_FOUND — corpus does not break out forging-tier suppliers
scores.interpretation: P&W supplies F135 (F-35), F119 (F-22), F100 (F-15/F-16); Rolls-Royce supplies V-22, F-35B lift fan, C-130J. These are all major forward-funded platforms in FY26 Pentagon books. ATI as a forging-tier supplier is genuinely diversified across these engine families. PASS.

scores.claim_text: ATI is positioned for multi-year next-generation jet engine + airframe demand via LTAs.
supports: pentagon_jbook(program_name='next-generation jet engine') NOT_FOUND — generic phrase, not a program name
scores.interpretation: Forward thesis without naming a specific program (NGAP, AETP, XA100, XA101, F-47 engine, etc.) is unverifiable at the J-Book PE level. The thesis is also primarily commercial (CFM RISE, GE9X-derivative, ultrafan) where J-Book doesn't apply. UNVERIFIABLE; not a red flag.

scores.claim_text: ATI operates an additive manufacturing facility in Margate, FL for A&D laser powder bed fusion.
supports: epa_frs returned 1 facility 'ATI ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING PRODUCTS' in MARGATE, FL — exact match
scores.interpretation: Facility verified in EPA Facility Registry Service. Real.

scores.claim_text: ATI maintains a US specialty-materials manufacturing footprint across PA, OR, NC, AL, NY, SC, WA, WI, CA.
supports: epa_frs PA returned 16 ATI facilities (incl. ATI ALLEGHENY LUDLUM in Latrobe, ATI FLAT ROLLED PRODUCTS in Monaca, ATI FLAT ROLLED PRODUCTS HOLDINGS LLC in Natrona Heights)
epa_frs OR returned 8 facilities (incl. ATI MILLERSBURG, ATI CAST PRODUCTS SALEM)
scores.interpretation: Domestic manufacturing footprint corroborated by EPA-FRS at scale. Zirconium/hafnium Millersburg facility specifically verified — critical for naval nuclear narrative.

scores.claim_text: ATI specialty-energy / naval-nuclear-adjacent revenue from zirconium/hafnium.
supports: usaspending found legacy Allegheny Ludlum DoD contract W15QKN08C0452 for '6A1-4V TITANIUM' ($1.44M) — confirms DoD direct-purchase relationship existed historically

usaspending search broad 'ATI Inc' returned 51 awards, $8.77M total — but most appear to be unrelated 'ATI'-named companies (GBI Cincinnati, etc.); ATI Inc's direct prime-contractor exposure to DoD is genuinely SMALL because ATI sells through primes
scores.M_value: n_awards=1 for 'Allegheny Technologies' ($1.44M titanium); n=0 for 'ATI Specialty Materials'
scores.interpretation: Direct prime-contractor DoD exposure is small by design — ATI is a Tier-2/Tier-3 materials supplier. The naval nuclear and military aero revenue flows through Bechtel/HII/Boeing/Lockheed/RTX/P&W/GE. This is the structural reason J-Book PE-level queries don't fire: ATI's defense revenue is distributed across many programs, none individually material enough to be a divergence target. PASS.

summary.framework_outcome: ATI is the WRONG TARGET for the J-Book divergence pattern by construction. The pattern flags small-caps whose forward revenue depends on a SPECIFIC, NAMED PE that the J-Book has zeroed. ATI is a $1.7B-debt, 7,600-employee specialty materials conglomerate with diversified A&D end-markets via prime relationships. The framework correctly produces 0 RED_FLAG / 0 SEVERE outcomes and routes the J-Book-grounded claims to UNVERIFIABLE (3) or PASS (corroborated via EPA-FRS / USAspending). This is a NEGATIVE-CONTROL pass for the J-Book detector.
